title: Build an agent-era blog system through the supervised Principal Workbench

mainline.contradiction: Design and implement a useful agent-era blog system from a blank product surface while proving that the Principal Workbench can expose, supervise, and redirect the real design-to-implementation process without inventing authority or hiding runtime drift.
acceptance: A from-scratch blog product has an explicit agent-era thesis, coherent interaction and information architecture, and one working end-to-end author-to-reader path verified in its own isolated Git project or worktree.
A live runner is bound to this exact Mission and the blog working site appears in the correct project projection without inferred worktree or Git-branch authority.
The Principal can observe bounded recent activity and at least one real intervention through the UI, with atomic target validation, an attributable receipt, and the resulting state change or failure.
The product and supervision experiment both record what the evidence admits, what remains unproven, and the reopening signal for another supervised or explicitly authorized unsupervised iteration.

options.label: Margin Ledger
options.immediateResult: Adopt a text-led editorial surface with source notes in a strong marginal column as the later UI direction; this run remains non-visual.
options.tradeoff: Source provenance is prominent, but the reading experience is denser and less calm.

options.label: Reading Field (recommended)
options.immediateResult: Adopt one spacious reading field for the canonical article and its derived lenses as the later UI direction; this run remains non-visual.
options.tradeoff: The canonical/projection distinction relies on disciplined hierarchy instead of a strong dashboard frame.

options.label: Quiet Instrument
options.immediateResult: Adopt an explicit instrument-like interface for switching among canonical, brief, and source-map views as the later UI direction; this run remains non-visual.
options.tradeoff: Operational state is easiest to inspect, but the product can feel more like a tool than a publication.

pendingDecisions.label: Authorize the declared DeepSeek disclosure
pendingDecisions.proposal: ALLOW — send only the declared categories to DeepSeek

options.label: Authorize DeepSeek
options.immediateResult: Start one supervised non-visual content-model run against the clean candidate worktree with the declared disclosure and write scope.
options.tradeoff: The declared project context leaves the local boundary and model usage may incur external cost.

options.label: Keep the external run blocked
options.immediateResult: Preserve the proposal and candidate worktree without sending project context or starting the runner.
options.tradeoff: The supervised system remains observable but its real implementation path is not yet tested.
